He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] out of high school. He was the second overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the Hornets. == Early life and high school career == Miller was born in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], grew up in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], and attended Cane Ridge High School.{{cite web |last=Spears |first=Joseph |date=March 9, 2021 |title=Brandon Miller, Cane Ridge headed to first basketball state tournament |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/03/09/brandon-miller-leads-cane-ridge-basketball-first-tssaa-state-tournament/4621166001/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=November 8, 2022 |work=[[The Tennessean]]}} He was named the Tennessee Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 23.3 points, eight rebounds, 4.3 assists, 2.6 blocks, and 2.3 steals per game during his junior season.{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=October 27, 2021 |title=KU Jayhawks basketball recruit Brandon Miller will pick college or pros next week |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article255317056.html |access-date=November 8, 2022 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]]}}{{cite web |last=Robinson |first=George |date=June 4, 2021 |title=Brandon Miller, Lashae Dwyer named Tennessee Gatorade basketball players of the year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/06/04/brandon-miller-lashae-dwyer-named-gatorade-tennessee-basketball-players-year/7546904002/ |access-date=November 8, 2022 |work=[[The Tennessean]]}} Miller repeated as the Gatorade Player of the Year and was named [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] as a senior after averaging 24.1 points, 8.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 2.3 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-signees-jaden-bradley-brandon-miller-named-mcdonalds-all-americans|title=Alabama Signees Jaden Bradley, Brandon Miller Named McDonald's All-Americans|first=Kate|last=Windham|website=[[SI.com]]|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}} He also played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and the [[McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Brandon Miller named Tennessee Gatorade boys basketball player of year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/03/16/brandon-miller-tennessee-gatorade-boys-basketball-player-year-alabama-signee/7063849001/ |access-date=March 28, 2023 |work=[[The Tennessean]]}} ===Recruiting=== Miller was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. His first scholarship offer was from [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]] who are coached by his cousin, [[Brian Collins (basketball)|Brian Collins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/09/08/tennessee-high-school-basketball-cane-ridge-brandon-miller-explains-his-final-four/5738899001/|title=Brandon Miller on G-League, TSU, not picking Tennessee Vols basketball|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=March 28, 2023}} On November 1, 2021, Miller committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] after considering offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and Tennessee State.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32527284|title=Top-15 forward Brandon Miller gives Alabama Crimson Tide second five-star commitment for 2022|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=November 1, 2021 |title=Brandon Miller commits to |access-date=November 8, 2022 |work=[[The Tennessean]]}} He also considered playing professionally in [[National Basketball League (Australia)|Australia's NBL]] or the [[G League Ignite]].{{cite web On December 17, 2022, Miller scored 36 points and six rebounds against [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].{{cite web |title=Gonzaga vs. Alabama - Men's Basketball 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401488386 |access-date=January 2, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} He posted an Alabama freshman-record 41 points on February 22, 2023, in a 78–76 overtime win against [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite news |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |title=Nate Oats defends Alabama response: 'Taking it very seriously' |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35727687 |access-date=February 24, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 24, 2023}} Miller was named the Most Valuable Player of the [[2023 SEC men's basketball tournament]] after averaging 20.3 points and 11 rebounds over three games.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/alabama-star-brandon-miller-named-most-valuable-player-in-sec-tournament.html|title=Alabama star Brandon Miller named most valuable player in SEC tournament|first=Nick|last=Alvarez|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 24, 2023}} He finished the season averaging an SEC-high 18.8 points per game and also averaged 8.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists. At the end of the regular season, Miller was named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]], the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]], and first-team All-Conference.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35804505|title=Alabama's Brandon Miller named top SEC player by coaches, AP|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}} He was a consensus second-team All-American selection after being selected to the first teams of the [[Associated Press]] and ''[[Sporting News]]'' and the second teams of [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] and [[USBWA]] selections.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/brandon-miller-is-alabamas-second-ever-consensus-second-team-all-american.html|title=Brandon Miller is Alabama's second-ever consensus second-team All-American|first=Mike|last=Rodak|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}} Miller was also named the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year]] and the [[NABC Freshman of the Year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/alabamas-brandon-miller-named-national-freshman-of-the-year-by-usbwa.html|title=Alabama's Brandon Miller named national freshman of the year by USBWA|first=Mike|last=Rodak|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 21, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/sports/brandon-miller-named-nabc-freshman-of-the-year/525-174b142d-dd22-4545-a03b-0c85abe103ca|title=Brandon Miller named NABC Freshman of the Year|first=Mo|last=Carter|website=[[WZDX|RocketCityNow.com]]|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}} Miller struggled in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], shooting just 19% from the field in Alabama's three games, the worst percentage by any player with 35 shot attempts in the tournament since 1985.{{Cite web|last=Nasser|first=Reese|date=March 24, 2023|title=Alabama's Brandon Miller hits rock bottom never seen in NCAA tournament history|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/alabamas-brandon-miller-hits-rock-bottom-never-seen-in-ncaa-tournament-history/ar-AA1935KU|access-date=March 25, 2023|website=MSN|language=en-US}} Alabama fell in the third round of the tournament to [[2022–23 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]], with Miller going 3-of-19 from the floor. After the season Miller announced that he would forgo the remainder of his collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36006157|title=Alabama freshman Brandon Miller entering 2023 NBA draft|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 30, 2023|access-date=March 30, 2023}} ==Professional career== The [[Charlotte Hornets]] selected Miller with the second overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37901730 |title=Hornets take Brandon Miller with 2nd pick of NBA draft|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 22, 2023}} On October 25, 2023, Miller made his NBA regular-season debut, scoring 13 points in a 116–110 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-brandon-miller-already-wants-more-after-nba-debut|title=Brandon Miller eager for more after encouraging Hornets NBA debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Donatien|first=Jerry|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}} On November 18, Miller scored a then career-high 29 points in a 122–108 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-brandon-miller-breakout-game-vs-knicks-draws-awesome-steve-clifford-review|title=Brandon Miller's big game for Hornets vs. Knicks draws awesome Steve Clifford review|website=ClutchPoints|last=Donatien|first=Jerry|date=November 18, 2023|access-date=November 18, 2023}} On January 29, 2024, Miller scored 29 points, tying his career high at the time, in a 113–92 loss to the New York Knicks.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-brandon-millers-big-game-in-lamelo-balls-absence-draws-rave-review|title=Hornets: Brandon Miller's big game in LaMelo Ball's absence draws rave review|website=ClutchPoints|last=Donatien|first=Jerry|date=January 29, 2024|access-date=January 29, 2024}} On February 4, Miller scored a then-career-high 35 points in a 115–99 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Pacers overcome career-high 35 points from Brandon Miller to beat Hornets 115-99|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585335|website=ESPN.com|date=February 4, 2024|access-date=February 6, 2024}} That record was upgraded to 38 points on November 21, 2024, when the team beat [[Detroit Pistons]] 123-121 in overtime.{{cite web |last=Roberts |first=Zach |date=November 22, 2024 |title=Hornets star Brandon Miller sets NBA record with career-best performance vs. Pistons |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hornets/news/hornets-star-brandon-miller-sets-nba-record-with-career-best-performance-vs-pistons |access-date=November 23, 2024 |website=si.com}} Miller started 27 games for Charlotte during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 21.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.6 assists. On January 23, 2025, Miller was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a [[scapholunate ligament injury|torn scapholunate ligament]] in his right wrist.{{Cite web|title=Hornets' Brandon Miller has season-ending wrist surgery|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43537216/hornets-brandon-miller-season-ending-wrist-surgery|access-date=January 25, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} Miller made 65 starts for the Hornets during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.3 assists. On May 6, 2026, Miller underwent surgery to address instability in his left shoulder.{{Cite web|title=Hornets' Brandon Miller has surgery for shoulder instability|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48696969/hornets-brandon-miller-surgery-shoulder-instability|access-date=May 20, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA .430 || .384 || .859 || 8.2 || 2.1 || .9 || .9 || 18.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Miller's father, Darrell Miller, played college football as a tight end at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] under head coach [[Gene Stallings]] in the early 1990s.{{cite web |last=Kelly |first=Nick |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Brandon Miller: Alabama basketball star grew up Tide fan in Tennessee |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/13/alabama-basketball-brandon-miller-stats-nick-saban-nate-oats/69786568007/ |access-date=March 28, 2023 |work=[[Tuscaloosa News]]}}{{cite web |title=Brandon Miller |url=https://rolltide.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brandon--miller/8260 |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=rolltide.com}} His older brother, Darrell Jr., played college basketball at [[Fisk University]] and professionally overseas. Miller's older sister, Britany, plays at [[Cumberland University]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4097532/2023/01/25/brandon-miller-alabama-nba-draft/|title=How Brandon Miller, Alabama basketball's star freshman, is mixing promise, production|first=Dana|last=O'Neil|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}} Miller revealed on an episode of [[Paul George]]'s podcast that his GOAT (for "Greatest Of All Time") is George and that he modeled his game after him.{{Cite magazine |last=Linn |first=Joey |date=July 17, 2023 |title=Brandon Miller Reveals Why Paul George is His GOAT |url=https://www.si.com/nba/clippers/news/brandon-miller-reveals-why-paul-george-is-his-goat |access-date=2024-01-29 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} ===Firearm incident=== On February 21, 2023, a Tuscaloosa police officer testified that Miller brought a firearm to teammate Darius Miles that was used in the fatal shooting of 23-year-old Jamea Jonae Harris in Tuscaloosa earlier that year.{{Cite web |date=February 21, 2023 |title=Police: Tide's Miller delivered gun used in shooting |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35707831 |access-date=February 22, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=February 22, 2023 |title=Alabama hoops star delivered gun in shooting, police say |url=https://apnews.com/article/Nate-Oats-Brandon-Miller-Alabama-Basketball-4efc92362b106b01ab0d0a2ee9a4ea6c |access-date=February 22, 2023 |website=AP News |language=en}} According to Miller's attorney, Miles had left the gun in Miller's vehicle after Miller dropped Miles off at a club. As Miller was on his way back to pick up Miles, Miles texted Miller, requesting that Miller bring Miles's gun. When Miller arrived, Miles told his friend Michael Davis that the gun was in the vehicle. Davis retrieved the gun and shot into a vehicle in which Harris was a passenger, while Harris's boyfriend returned fire, resulting in two bullets striking Miller's car. Miller's attorney stated that Miller had no knowledge of any intent to use the weapon.{{cite web |last=Rodak |first=Mike |date=February 22, 2023 |title=Brandon Miller 'never touched the gun' used in Darius Miles capital murder case, attorney says |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/02/attorney-says-brandon-miller-never-knew-illegal-activity-would-occur.html |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=al.com}} According to the Tuscaloosa police officer's testimony, while Miles and Davis initially lied to officers about the incident, Miller's account of the shooting almost exactly matched what investigators gathered from video evidence and other witness testimony.{{cite web |last=Rodak |first=Mike |date=February 22, 2023 |title=Alabama Basketball Alabama AD: Nate Oats did not have complete information about Brandon Miller |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/02/alabama-ad-nate-oats-did-not-have-complete-information-about-brandon-miller.html |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=al.com}} Tuscaloosa County chief deputy district attorney Paula Whitley stated Miller would face no charges as a result of the incident. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links==
